Chorus.what: The Chorus enters singing of Dionysus's birth and the joy of the mountain rites.
The Chorus calls on the god to come, then falls to the ground at the earthquake.
The Chorus sings of freedom, God's slow judgment of the proud, and happy life.
The Chorus calls for vengeance on Pentheus and hails Agave as she enters with his head.

Dionysus.what: Dionysus declares he has come to Thebes disguised as a man to punish Pentheus and the women.
Disguised as a Lydian stranger, Dionysus answers Pentheus calmly and warns of the god's vengeance.
Dionysus shakes the palace with earthquake and fire, escapes, and bewitches Pentheus into spying on the women.
Dionysus dresses the maddened Pentheus as a Bacchanal and leads him toward doom.
Dionysus lures Pentheus up the pine and pronounces doom on Cadmus and Agave.

Pentheus.what: Pentheus rages against the new god, orders Teiresias's seat wrecked and the stranger captured.
Pentheus questions the stranger, cuts his hair, takes his staff, and imprisons him in the stable.
Pentheus finds Dionysus free, calls out his army, then is bewitched into spying on the women.
Pentheus, maddened, is dressed as a woman and leaves to spy on the Maenads.
Pentheus is set in a pine on Kithaeron and torn apart by the Maenads.

Agave.what: Agave tears Pentheus apart, returns with his head as a lion's, and wakes to horror.

Cadmus.what: Cadmus prepares with Teiresias to dance in Bacchic dress and urges Pentheus to accept Dionysus.
Cadmus brings the body, restores Agave's sanity, laments, and hears his serpent doom.

Leader.what: The Leader calls on the god to destroy Pentheus and demands the Messenger's story.

Messenger.what: The herdsman describes the Bacchae's miracles on Kithaeron and urges Pentheus to accept the god.
The Messenger reports how Pentheus was lured up a pine and torn apart.

Soldier.what: The Soldier brings in the bound Dionysus and reports the escape of the imprisoned maidens.

Teiresias.what: Teiresias urges Pentheus to accept Dionysus and prepares with Cadmus to go dance.
